title: Sum of Left Leaves
prompt:
Given the `root` of a binary tree, return the sum of all values of nodes that are left leaves. A left leaf is a node with no children that is the left child of its parent.

The tree is given as a level-order array where `null` marks a missing child (the standard LeetCode serialization). Your function receives this array directly; the starter code includes a helper that builds the tree from it, so you only need to compute the sum.

examples.explanation: The only left leaf is 9 (child of 3) ... wait, 15 is a left leaf too: 9 + 15 = 24.
The root has no parent, so even though it's a leaf, it can't be a left leaf.
The only leaf (2) is a right child, not a left child, so it doesn't contribute to the sum.

constraints: The number of nodes is in the range [1, 1000]
hints: You can't tell if a node is a leaf just by looking at it in isolation — you need to check from the parent whether the left child has no children of its own.

While traversing, whenever you visit a node and look at its left child, check whether that left child is itself a leaf (no left and no right child); if so, add its value directly instead of recursing further.
For every other case (a left child that isn't a leaf, or the right child in general), just recurse normally and sum the results from both subtrees.

solution.approach: Recurse through the tree; at each node, inspect its left child. If the left child exists and is itself a leaf (no children), add its value directly to the running sum. Otherwise, recurse into the left child normally to keep searching deeper. Always recurse into the right child normally, since a right child can never itself be a left leaf, but its subtree might contain some.
